hookups.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('Camping is primitive, temporary and dispersed. There are no established campsites and no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations).'), read 2026-10-21

facilities.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Chickahominy lists Primitive Camping among its activities; its map shows a parking area at the river end of the road just north-east of Eagle Bottom, with no boat ramp there (the WMA's ramp is on Morris Creek).

booking.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ + https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/chickahominy/ (Recreational Opportunities: 'Primitive Camping'; Facilities; map), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Chickahominy page that primitive camping is still allowed on the WMA, and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. The riverside parking spot near Eagle Bottom is not at the boat ramp (Morris Creek), and DWR's 300-ft rule names lakes and facilities, not rivers, so no waterfront conflict found. Not stated: season. Note left as is.
